FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
Steady red means stop and wait for green, while flashing red means stop and then proceed when clear, just as at a stop sign. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F08 vs sec05-F16. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
Flashing yellow light and flashing yellow arrow differ: the plain flashing light warns of a hazard, while the flashing arrow permits a left turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and walkers. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty three; confusable sec05-F17 vs sec05-F15. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A01
Right on red is allowed at most intersections after a full stop, but left on red works only when turning from one one-way street into a second one. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty three; confusable sec05-F08 vs sec05-F09. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A01
If the green arrow goes out but the round green remains, the turn is still allowed, now only after yielding; a red arrow means no turn that way at all. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty three; prereq sec05-F13 and sec05-F12. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A01
A dark or broken signal is handled as a four-way stop, not as a green light for the busier road. [A01]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty two; prereq sec05-F07. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A01
The stopping point at a stop sign follows an order: the stop line first, then the near-side crosswalk, then the spot nearest the cross road with a view of traffic. [A01]
Why it matters: group signs; difficulty two; prereq sec05-F22. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A02
Warning signs are yellow or fluorescent green, work zone signs are orange, guide signs are green, service signs are blue and recreation signs are brown. [A02]
Why it matters: group signs; difficulty two; confusable sec05-F28 vs sec05-F32 vs sec05-F33 vs sec05-F34. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A02
A One Way sign tells you which single direction a street allows, while Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs tell a driver already facing the wrong direction to go no further. [A02]
Why it matters: group signs; difficulty one; confusable sec05-F25 vs sec05-F24. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0011]

Misconception: a right turn on red needs no stop; you must stop and yield first. [A01]
Misconception: a yellow light means speed up to beat the red; it means stop unless you are already in the intersection. [A01]
Misconception: a rear-view camera replaces looking back; it is used in addition to mirrors and an over-the-shoulder check. [A01]
Misconception: you can shift gears on railroad tracks to get across faster; shifting there risks a stall. [A02]
Mnemonic: Flashing red, act like a stop sign; flashing yellow, slow and go with care. [A01]
Mnemonic: Orange for work, green to guide, blue for service, brown for parks and history. [A02]
Glossary: HAWK signal means a High Intensity Activated Crosswalk signal that flashes yellow and red so pedestrians can cross. [A01]
Glossary: Regulatory sign means a black or red on white sign stating a law that applies at that spot. [A01]
Glossary: ENS sign means the blue railroad emergency notification system sign posted at a highway-rail grade crossing. [A02]
Glossary: Advisory speed means a cautionary safe speed for a curve, corner or ramp in ideal conditions. [A02]
